advances: Common affine normal form and enclosing simplex. Zero capture by itself does not force facet contact, and a saturated A cut is outside the capacity assertion.

proof: Every interior point of $B$ has strictly negative margin in every row, since a nonzero continuous normal with a nonnegative margin at an interior point would capture positive volume. Their positive weighted sum at base $1$ is $D$, hence $D<0$. After the rescaling the continuous normals $v_i$ sum to zero, still have rank $d$, and the new base coefficients $t_i$ sum to $-(d+1)$. The map $q\mapsto(v_i\cdot q)_i$ is bijective onto the sum-zero subspace, by rank and the zero normal sum. Solve $v_i\cdot q=-1-t_i$ simultaneously. The resulting shear gives the displayed cap forms. It is a translation on each fiber and keeps the midpoint inclusion. Closedness and the zero captured volume place $B$ in every halfspace $v_i\cdot x'\le1$. The affine map $x'\mapsto((1-v_i\cdot x')/(d+1))_i$ is a bijection onto the coordinate-sum-one hyperplane and takes the enclosing polytope onto the standard simplex. It sends zero to the standard centroid. Positive rescaling and the shear induce invertible changes of cap-normal parameters near each fixed-mark cap. Thus the fixed-mark proper/zero criticality lemma applies to the corresponding proper rows. In the transformed coordinates the three cutting levels are $-1,0,1$, respectively, and fiber translations preserve section area.
statement: In the compatible three-fiber setting at bases $-1,0,1$ in continuous dimension $d\ge2$, let $d+1$ caps through $(0,y)$ have margins $u_i\cdot(x-y)+\alpha_i z$, where the $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and $\lambda_i>0$ satisfy $\sum_i\lambda_i u_i=0$. Suppose each cap captures zero $d$-volume from the positive-volume fiber $B$ at base $1$. Then $D=\sum_i\lambda_i\alpha_i<0$. Multiply margin $i$ by $(d+1)\lambda_i/(-D)$. After a single shear $x'=x-y-qz$ the caps become $v_i\cdot x'\ge z$ with $\sum_i v_i=0$. The transformed $B$ lies in the simplex $\{x':v_i\cdot x'\le1\ \forall i\}$, whose centroid is zero. For each cap that is locally minimizing through $y\in\operatorname{int}K$ and has proper $A$ capture, the transformed $B$ section is a positive-area facet of $B$ with area at least the area of the $A$ section, and their Minkowski midpoint lies in the corresponding $K$ section with the same Brunn–Minkowski capacity bound.
title: One shear for a full-rank zero-endpoint cap circuit
